Two concurrent callers — the hourly `Jobs::PollFeed` and a user-triggered `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (or two concurrent `EmbedController#best` requests for the same un-embedded URL) — can both see `embed.blank?` and both attempt the insert. The loser raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` from `create!`, which is an unhandled exception on this path; `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` even guards with an `exists?` check (lib/topic_retriever.rb:37/42) that is itself a check-then-act race. finding.suggestionContent: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases only the stored column, but the comparison value `host` comes from `uri.host` unmodified. URL hosts are case-insensitive, so an embed/referer URL with an uppercase host (e.g. `http://EVILTROUT.com`) produces `uri.host == "EVILTROUT.com"`, which never equals `lower("eviltrout.com")`, and the legitimate host is rejected as not embeddable. Downcase the extracted host before the query, e.g. `where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase)`.

finding.suggestionContent: The device limit can be bypassed because `tagDeviceUI` writes the cache entry (`a.localCache.SetDefault(key, ...)`) before calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, so when the store returns the new `ErrDeviceLimitReached` this error propagates (this line) and blocks only the first request; every subsequent request from the same device hits the cache at impl.go:83, `TagDevice` returns nil, and `Anonymous.Authenticate` issues a valid identity. This lets a device that was rejected at the limit authenticate on retry for the full cache TTL (~29 min), defeating the new limit control. Only set the cache entry after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns success (or delete the key on error).

Enforce the count and insert inside a single transaction (e.g. row lock / `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the count) so the limit is not overshot under concurrency.

This adds DB latency to the anonymous auth hot path; run the tagging asynchronously (with a bounded background context) when the limit is not configured, or otherwise avoid the blocking COUNT query on the critical path.

finding.suggestionContent: The device limit is enforced with a non-atomic check-then-act: `CountDevices` is called and, only if `count >= s.deviceLimit`, does the code take the update-only path. Concurrent anonymous requests from new devices can all read `count < deviceLimit` before any of them inserts, so each falls through to the INSERT ... ON CONFLICT branch and creates a new row. The `anon_device` table has no constraint that could make this atomic, so `deviceLimit` is not a hard bound — it can be exceeded by the number of in-flight requests. If the limit is meant to be a real invariant, enforce it atomically (e.g. a guarded INSERT/`INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < limit`, or a serialized/transactional check) rather than counting in a separate statement.

finding.suggestionContent: The prefix/suffix trimming loops are unbounded relative to each other: the `end` loop condition only checks `end < sanitized.length() && end < value.length()`, never that `end` stays below the region already consumed by `start`. When the sanitizer removes characters and the text around the removal repeats (e.g. value="abbba" sanitized to "abba"), start and end both walk the whole string, so start + end > value.length() and `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException (same for the sanitized.substring call). The `!Objects.equals(sanitized, value)` guard only proves the strings differ, not that the ranges are valid. Since verify() (lines 48-54) only catches IOException, this unchecked exception escapes and fails the build with an opaque error instead of a useful message. Bound both loops so they cannot overlap, e.g. add `start + end < value.length()` / `start + end < sanitized.length()` to the while conditions.

finding.suggestionContent: `santizeAnchors` advances `englishMatcher` once per iteration of `matcher` and compares `matcher.group()` against `englishMatcher.group()`, assuming the i-th anchor in the translation corresponds to the i-th anchor in the English source. Nothing guarantees that ordering (a translation may omit an earlier anchor, insert one, or reorder them), so after the first divergence every later anchor is compared to the wrong English tag and valid translations are reported as "Didn't find anchor tag". Additionally, the removal is done with `value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` on the already-mutated string and by literal text rather than at the current `matcher` position, so when the same anchor text occurs more than once it strips the wrong occurrence and the value handed to `policy.sanitize(value)` no longer lines up with what the matcher scanned. Remove the matched region via the matcher itself (e.g. rebuild the string with `matcher.start()/end()` on the current match, or match English anchors by set/identity rather than by positional zip) so the compared and removed anchor are the same one.

finding.suggestionContent: `santizeAnchors` advances `englishMatcher` once per iteration of `matcher` and compares `matcher.group()` against `englishMatcher.group()`, assuming the i-th anchor in the translation corresponds to the i-th anchor in the English source. Nothing guarantees that ordering (a translation may omit an earlier anchor, insert one, or reorder them), so after the first divergence every later anchor is compared to the wrong English tag and valid translations are reported as "Didn't find anchor tag". Additionally, the removal is done with `value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` on the already-mutated string and by literal text rather than at the current `matcher` position, so when the same anchor text occurs more than once it strips the wrong occurrence and the value handed to `policy.sanitize(value)` no longer lines up with what the matcher scanned. Remove the matched region via the matcher itself (e.g. rebuild the string with `matcher.start()/end()` on the current match, or match English anchors by set/identity rather than by positional zip) so the compared and removed anchor are the same one.
